sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head pale yellowish brown; wings pale yellow; body paler than the head. Head and body densely covered with hairs, interspersed with long setae; wing hairs weak, densely covered with minute spines. Body length (with wings) about 9.5-10.01 mm, without wings 4.5-6.0 mm. Head capsule subquadrate, sides parallel; width 0.80-0.85 mm, length to mandible base 0.80-0.90 mm. Fontanelle minute, situated in the middle of the vertex. Compound eyes small, oval (0.20-0.23 × 0.17-0.20 mm), weakly projecting; their distance from the lower margin of the head less than their short diameter. Ocelli very small, oval (length 0.05-0.08 mm), situated from the compound eye a distance equal to their long diameter. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 3 longer than segment 2; segment 4 equal in length to segment 2. Postclypeus weakly inflated, length less than half its width. Mandibles of the typical Heterotermes type. Pronotum trapezoidal; disc with a pale T-shaped mark, lateral margins and angles rounded; length greater than half its width, narrower than the head; length 0.45-0.53 mm, width 0.68-0.70 mm; anterior margin weakly incurved in the middle and slightly raised; posterior margin not distinctly notched. Wings delicate, whitish. Forewing length 7.5-8.0 mm; cubitus sending 10-12 branches to the posterior margin. Hindwing length 7.0 mm; cubitus sending 9-11 branches to the posterior margin. Abdomen long, densely hairy; cerci 2-segmented, 0.88 mm long. Stylus of the male single-segmented, 0.05 mm long.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: head capsule yellow to yellowish brown; body paler; mandibles dark brown. Cephalic hairs sparse, body hairs denser. Body length about 4.5-6.0 mm. Head capsule subrectangular, cylindrical; much longer than wide, length to mandible base 1.38-1.69 mm, about 1.5 times the width (0.85-1.0 mm) or a little more; sides nearly straight; posterior part rounded. Fontanelle minute, circular, opening at the end of a small tube in the anterior third of the vertex. Compound eyes and ocelli absent. Antennae 14-segmented; segment 2 longer than segment 3, segment 3 the shortest. Anteclypeus transparent, hairless; postclypeus hairy, concolorous with the frons, separated from it by a weak line. Labrum nearly triangular, apex acute, reaching two-thirds of the mandibles. Mandibles long (0.80-0.85 mm), sword-shaped; length about half to slightly less than two-thirds of the head length without mandibles; left mandible with a large basal swelling and 4 teeth on the basal half; right mandible with 1-2 weak teeth on the broad base. Postmentum long, clavate; narrowest beyond the middle; length 0.80-1.25 mm, greatest width 0.35-0.45 mm, waist width 0.15-0.20 mm. Pronotum flat, subreniform; narrower than the head, length slightly more than half its width; length 0.38-0.50 mm, width 0.63-0.75 mm; anterior margin weakly incurved in the middle, posterior margin straight or weakly incurved. Legs slender; tibial spurs 3:2:2; tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen elongate-oval; cerci short, 2-segmented; stylus single-segmented, finger-like. Minor soldier: smaller than the major soldier. Body length 3.0-4.0 mm, head length to mandible base 1.23 mm, head width 0.80 mm, pronotal width 0.57 mm. Antennae 13-14-segmented. Otherwise as in the major soldier.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow to yellowish; body paler. Head and body rather densely hairy. Body length about 3.00-5.00 mm. Head capsule subquadrate, width about equal to the length to the mandible base; length to mandible base 0.80 mm, width 0.80-0.85 mm. Fontanelle indistinct. Compound eyes and ocelli absent. Antennae 13-14-segmented; segment 2 equal to segments 3 and 4 together. Postclypeus weakly inflated, shorter than half its width. Mandibles as in the alate. Pronotum as in the soldier, but the anterior margin with a deep median notch. Legs and abdomen as in the soldier.

note: Rewritten from the species-level description of Roonwal & Chhotani (1989); the original is in English. Alate, major soldier, minor soldier, worker and distribution are all covered. The last digit of the alate body length "with wings c 9.5-10.01" is reproduced as in the source OCR and is probably 9.5-10.0, but has not been changed. The source is a two-column OCR and still contains some garbled characters (typically/feferote/wej-type, wlLtish, Irons, cerd, b^ of mandibles, etc.); none of them affects the figures, and they are not marked individually.
